---
title: "Desktop"
subtitle: "A fake desktop with wallpaper, menubar and dock — launch as many windows as you like."
quarto-os:
  vm:
    asset-base: vm-assets/
    setup: |
      mkdir -p ~/lab3
      cd ~/lab3
      printf '# Lab 3 — pipes\n\nCount the words in poem.txt, then find the longest line.\n' > TASK.md
      printf 'Roses are red,\nviolets are blue,\nbash pipes are neat,\nand so are you.\n' > poem.txt
---

A desktop is a fenced div with the class `.os-desktop`. It draws a wallpaper, a menubar
and a dock; windows nested inside it float at their `x`/`y` position, can be dragged,
minimized, maximized and closed.

## A first desktop {#first}

````markdown
::: {#demo .os-desktop height="460px"}

::: {.os-window title="Read me" x=24 y=24 width=330 height=230}
Click the icons in the **dock** …
:::

::: {.os-window title="sunset.svg" x=390 y=60 width=360}
![](assets/sunset.svg)
:::

:::
````

::: {#demo .os-desktop height="460px"}

::: {.os-window title="Read me" x=24 y=24 width=330 height=230}
#### Hello, desktop!

Click the icons in the **dock** below. Every click opens a **new instance** — open three
terminals if you like. All of them share one Linux VM.
:::

::: {.os-window title="sunset.svg" x=390 y=60 width=360}
![](assets/sunset.svg){fig-alt="Illustration of a sunset over hills"}
:::

:::

The dock shows `terminal,vscode,explorer` by default; choose your own with
`dock="terminal,explorer"` (or `dock=""` for none). The VM only boots when the first VM
app is opened, so a desktop with just content windows costs nothing.

## Launch buttons {#launchers}

A span with the class `.os-launch` becomes a button that opens a new window. With
`target="demo"` the windows open on the desktop above; any window attribute can be
passed along:

::: {.launch-row}
[New terminal]{.os-launch app="terminal" target="demo" cwd="~/lab3"}
[Terminal running `ls -l`]{.os-launch app="terminal" target="demo" cwd="~/lab3" run="ls -l" title="ls"}
[VS Code]{.os-launch app="vscode" target="demo" folder="~/lab3" open="TASK.md"}
[Explorer]{.os-launch app="explorer" target="demo" path="~/lab3"}
[Browser]{.os-launch app="browser" target="demo" url="windows.html" title="Content windows"}
:::

```markdown
[New terminal]{.os-launch app="terminal" target="demo" cwd="~/lab3"}
[VS Code]{.os-launch app="vscode" target="demo" folder="~/lab3" open="TASK.md"}
[Explorer]{.os-launch app="explorer" target="demo" path="~/lab3"}
[Browser]{.os-launch app="browser" target="demo" url="windows.html"}
```

::: {.callout-note}
The `browser` app shows a page in an iframe. On pages that use the VM, only same-origin
pages (like another page of your site) and sites that allow cross-origin embedding
load — see [Limitations](../index.qmd#limitations).
:::

## Wallpaper, menubar & window states {#custom}

Set a `wallpaper` image, the app name shown in the `title` of the menubar, and pick the
dock icons. Windows can start `minimized` or `maximized` with `state`:

````markdown
::: {.os-desktop height="420px" title="Lab 3" wallpaper="assets/wallpaper.svg" dock="terminal,explorer"}

::: {.os-window app="terminal" x=30 y=30 width=520 height=260 cwd="~/lab3" run="cat TASK.md" theme="dark"}
:::

::: {.os-window title="Hint" state="minimized" x=420 y=120 width=300}
Try `wc -w poem.txt` and `awk '{ print length, $0 }' poem.txt | sort -n | tail -1`.
:::

:::
````

::: {#lab .os-desktop height="420px" title="Lab 3" wallpaper="assets/wallpaper.svg" dock="terminal,explorer"}

::: {.os-window app="terminal" title="bash — lab3" x=30 y=30 width=520 height=260 cwd="~/lab3" run="cat TASK.md" theme="dark"}
:::

::: {.os-window title="Hint" state="minimized" x=420 y=120 width=320}
Try `wc -w poem.txt` and

`awk '{ print length, $0 }' poem.txt | sort -n | tail -1`
:::

:::

The *Hint* window starts minimized — restore it from the dock when a student is stuck.

## A full-height student workspace {#workspace}

For labs and exercises, give students a whole screen: a desktop that fills the window
(`height="calc(100vh - 120px)"`, page-wide with Quarto's `.column-screen-inset`) with
VS Code, a terminal and the Explorer already open.

````markdown
::: {.column-screen-inset}
::: {#workspace .os-desktop height="calc(100vh - 120px)" title="Workspace"}

::: {.os-window app="vscode" x=16 y=16 width=660 height=540 folder="~/lab3" open="TASK.md,poem.txt"}
:::

::: {.os-window app="terminal" x=692 y=16 width=520 height=300 cwd="~/lab3"}
:::

::: {.os-window app="explorer" x=692 y=332 width=520 height=224 path="~/lab3"}
:::

:::
:::
````

::: {.column-screen-inset .workspace-full}
::: {#workspace .os-desktop height="calc(100vh - 120px)" title="Workspace"}

::: {.os-window app="vscode" title="lab3 — VS Code" x=16 y=16 width=660 height=540 folder="~/lab3" open="TASK.md,poem.txt"}
:::

::: {.os-window app="terminal" title="bash — lab3" x=692 y=16 width=520 height=300 cwd="~/lab3"}
:::

::: {.os-window app="explorer" title="lab3" x=692 y=332 width=520 height=224 path="~/lab3"}
:::

:::
:::

Everything on this page — the three desktops, every terminal, editor and explorer —
runs on the **same** VM: a file saved in the workspace's VS Code shows up in the Lab 3
terminal above.
